facts.fact: An NPS Vatsalya account is opened and operated by the minor's parent or legal guardian, for the minor's exclusive benefit until 18
facts.quote: Parents or legal guardians can open and manage the NPS Vatsalya account on behalf of the minor. The account shall be operated by the guardian for the exclusive benefit of the minor until the attainment of age of majority (18 years).

facts.fact: The account (PRAN) is in the minor's name
facts.quote: Yes, a unique Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) in the name of the minor subscriber will be issued by the CRA upon opening the account.

facts.fact: It is open to all Indian citizens under 18
facts.quote: NPS Vatsalya is open to all Indian citizens under 18 years of age. The account will be opened and operated by the guardian on behalf of the minor.

facts.fact: NRIs and OCIs under 18 can also join
facts.quote: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs) under 18 years of age can join the scheme.

facts.fact: A grandparent can open it only as a court-appointed legal guardian, submitting a copy of the court order with their own KYC documents; the FAQ makes no other provision for grandparents
facts.quote: Yes, in case a legal guardian has been appointed by a court, a copy of the relevant court order must be submitted along with the KYC documents of the guardian.
facts.note: The grandparent rule is derived: the FAQ lets only 'parents or legal guardians' open the account and gives the court-order requirement for a court-appointed guardian; it does not mention grandparents.

facts.fact: Relatives and friends (e.g. a grandparent who is not the guardian) can make gift contributions to the account
facts.quote: 3. Gift Contributions In addition to Parents/guardians, relatives and friends can gift contributions to the NPS Vatsalya account.

facts.fact: Minimum contribution to open the account is Rs 250
facts.quote: The minimum contribution for account opening is ₹250/-.
There is no limit on the maximum amount for contributions.

facts.fact: There is no limit on the number of contributions in a year
facts.quote: No, there are no restrictions on the number of contributions in a year.

facts.fact: The NPS Trust FAQ giving these rules is updated as on 16.06.2026
Document: proof of the minor's date of birth (e.g. birth certificate, school leaving certificate, minor PAN or passport)
facts.quote: Proof of date of birth of the minor (Birth Certificate, School Leaving Certificate, Matriculation Certificate, Minor Permanent Account Number (PAN), or Passport); AND
KYC of the guardian (Aadhaar, Driving License, Passport, Voter ID card, National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) Job Card, or National Population Register documents);

facts.fact: Document: PAN of the guardian or Form 60
facts.quote: iii. PAN of the guardian or Form 60 declaration as per Rule 114B

facts.fact: The guardian is automatically the nominee
facts.quote: No, the guardian automatically becomes the nominee under the scheme.

facts.fact: Only one account can be opened per child
facts.quote: The guardian can open only one account for each minor/child.

facts.fact: It can be opened offline at PoPs registered with PFRDA, through PoPs' online facility, or on the eNPS platform
facts.quote: Offline: Points of Presence (POPs) registered with PFRDA • Online facility provided by PoPs • eNPS platform (https://npstrust.org.in/open-nps-vatsalya)

facts.fact: The PoPs include major banks and India Post
facts.quote: These PoPs include major banks, India Post, and pension funds, with both online and physical modes available for account setup.

summary: All NPS Vatsalya facts confirmed on the NPS Trust FAQ updated 16.06.2026 (Rs 250 opening/annual, no max, guardian rules, documents, one account, nominee), the NPS Trust page (gift contributions) and PIB (banks, India Post as PoPs).
